_comment: Indexes that predate the migration ledger (declared in a table's original CREATE TABLE definition, so they legitimately have no dated migration). Consumed by sql-schema-index-parity.test.js to guard the definition->ledger direction: any NEW index added to a src/sql/<table>.sql definition must either be created by a dated migration under src/sql/migrations/ OR added here deliberately. This is the index twin of test/fixtures/schema-baseline.json (#3386). Regenerating this file in the same commit that adds the index silently waives the guard - review baseline diffs. A table CREATEd by a dated migration does NOT belong here: its indexes are ledger-covered by that CREATE TABLE. ENTRY FORMAT (#4435): each entry is {name, columns, unique} - the index name plus its normalized column list (order and (len) prefix preserved) and UNIQUE flag - not a bare name. The shape is asserted by sql-schema-index-parity.test.js, so re-pointing or re-prefixing a pre-ledger index fails until a dated migration ships and this file is deliberately re-frozen.
_why_it_matters: An inline KEY / UNIQUE KEY added to a definition AFTER the table already exists reaches nobody: reconcileTableIndexes self-heals only standalone CREATE INDEX (parseExpectedIndexes never parses an inline KEY), so a running node cannot back-fill it and a migration-replayed replica never receives it. Such an index exists on fresh installs only. Ship a dated migration for it, or declare it standalone so the reconciler can heal it.
_known_unledgered_comment: Indexes present in a definition today with no migration that are KNOWN debt awaiting their own migration. The test skips these but keeps them visible. Delete each entry when its migration ships. Empty = no outstanding debt.
